---
title: "Recipe 8 — Run the CRS differential and the bench harness on your own node"
---

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/bench-vm.sh`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/bench-vm.sh) + [`test/crs-differential`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/test/crs-differential), Linux VM, root | Bench | hard | 45 min | bench · crs | bench, budgets, walls |

### Problem

You want the full suite under the CI shape on the node you own. You want the
verdict walls measured against the [spec 17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#17-performance-targets--benchmark-plan)
budgets, and the CRS posture re-checked on the same node.

### Solution

1. Run the CRS parity gate first (any host with Go):

```bash
go test ./test/crs-differential/ -run TestCorpusParity -count=1
```

2. Run the bench rig inside a Linux VM copy of the tree (root):

```bash
sudo bash lab/bench-vm.sh
```

3. Read the four sections the rig prints:

```text
== G: full suite, new CI shape (p 1 + no_regex_multiline)
== H: old CI shape control (parallel, GOMAXPROCS=4)
== I: bench verdict walls, new CI shape
== J: prefilter-off control (same shape, directive removed)
```

The wall lines carry one row per measured scenario:

```text
MEASURED <scenario> n=<n> size=<bytes> p50=<us> p99=<us> budget=<name> (<budget-hint us>) factor=<x>x
```

### Discussion

Section G runs the suite serialized (`-p 1`) with the `no_regex_multiline` build
tag; the CI fleet runs this shape. Section H runs the parallel-shape control;
the delta shows what the serialization buys. Section I measures the live-path verdict walls against the named budget. The `factor` value reads the wall at 1.00x. Section J removes the `SecRxPreFilter On`
directive and re-measures; the delta prices the prefilter. The rig restores the
directive on exit.

A wall above 1.00x is a budget miss on your node. The hosted CI certifies the
budgets; read the VM as the A and B surface. The parity gate from Recipe 5 rides
the same tree: run it again after any rule or exclusion change.
